# @peektravel/app-utilities

> Dependency-light TypeScript library wrapping the Peek "backoffice" GraphQL
> gateway. Callers only touch `PeekAccessService`, the per-resource services it
> hands out, and clean data-model types — never raw GraphQL. Ships dual ESM+CJS
> with bundled `.d.ts`. Only runtime dependency: `jsonwebtoken`.

The authoritative, always-in-sync contract is the bundled type declarations
(`dist/index.d.ts`) — read them via go-to-definition. This file is a map; the
`.d.ts` and `README.md` (also shipped) have full detail and examples.

## Entry point

Construct one `PeekAccessService` per install, then call `get<Resource>Service()`
accessors (each memoized, bound to a shared authenticated transport that mints
and caches a short-lived JWT).

```ts
import { PeekAccessService } from "@peektravel/app-utilities";

const peek = new PeekAccessService({
  installId,   // JWT subject
  jwtSecret,   // HMAC secret signing the JWT
  issuer,      // app name (JWT issuer)
  apiUrl,      // the install webhook's apiUrl — the app endpoint, used as given
  // optional: gatewayKey, tokenTtlSeconds, tokenRefreshLeewaySeconds,
  // retryDelaysMs, logger, fetch, itemOptionsPageSize,
  // accessOptions: { fullCustomerAccess: false }  // default — see "Access options / PII"
});
```

Targeting an install by URL: pass the install webhook's `apiUrl` as the config
`apiUrl` — for Peek it is the **sole** request URL (every call POSTs to it,
unmodified); for CNG/ACME it is the base and the REST path is appended. No
app-id/gateway segment is inserted (`appId` is unused). Any app id in the path is
the registry's own traffic tag, opaque to callers. `createAccessServiceForInstall(install, config)`
builds the right service for `install.platform` (`peek`/`cng`/`acme`) wired to
`install.apiUrl` in one call (throws on unknown/`null` platform). `appId` +
`baseUrl` (and the hardcoded gateway default) are **`@deprecated`** — they
reconstruct the URL with a compiled-in default that can't be right for every
install; the fallbacks will be removed and a URL will become **required**.

## Access options / PII — `fullCustomerAccess`

**The most commonly-misunderstood option in this package. Read this before
debugging "why is `customerName` null?" or "why did `makePayment` throw?".**

Every access service takes `accessOptions?: AccessOptions`
(`{ fullCustomerAccess?: boolean }`). It is passed **once at construction**, not
per call, and applies to every service that access service hands out.

```ts
const peek = new PeekAccessService({
  installId, jwtSecret, issuer, appId, gatewayKey,
  accessOptions: { fullCustomerAccess: true },  // opt in to PII + payment ops
});
```

- **Default is `false` (PII off).** Omitting `accessOptions`, passing `{}`, or
  passing `undefined` are all identical to `{ fullCustomerAccess: false }`.
- There is **no per-call override** by design — an install either has customer-
  data entitlement or it doesn't. Need both modes? Construct two access services.
- Consumed by `BookingService` and `ReviewService`; `parseWaiverWebhook(body,
  options?)` takes the same object directly. `CngAccessService` /
  `AcmeAccessService` accept the field but have no PII surface (inert).

### With `fullCustomerAccess: false` (default) — two distinct effects

**1. PII is never requested.** Filtering happens in the GraphQL selection, so the
data never leaves the gateway; the fields simply arrive as `null`/empty in the
clean models. There is no error and no warning — a missing name looks exactly
like a customer who didn't provide one.

| Surface | Redacted (→ `null`/empty) | Always present |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Booking | primary-guest `customerName`/`email`/`phone`/`postalCode`/`isGdpr`/opt-ins; per-guest identity (name, country, DOB, email, phone, postal code, `isGdpr`, custom `fieldResponses`) — guests keep only ids + participation/opt-in flags; booking- and ticket-level custom `questionAnswers`; the customer `portalUrl` | notes, Peek Pro operator deep link, money/price breakdown, resources, timeslot + structural ids |
| Review | reviewer `customerName` / `customerEmail` | comment, rating, dates, credited guides |
| Waiver webhook | participant `guestName`, signed-document `fileUrl` (redacted at parse time — the payload is fixed, so there is no selection to trim) | signature/agreement ids, timestamps, booking linkage |

**2. Payment & booking-modification operations are disabled.** These throw
`PiiAccessDisabledError` (exported; `.operation` names the blocked method)
**before any network call**:

`getPaymentsOnFile`, `makePayment`, `refund`, `createInvoiceLink`, `addAddon`,
`removeAddon`.

Still available without the flag: `create` (**including `markAsPaid`**),
`getById`, `getGuests`, `searchByTimeRange`, `searchByTimeslot`, `listAddons`,
`cancel`, `appendNote`, `setCheckinStatus`, and every other resource service.

### Choosing a value

Leave it `false` for operations/logistics tooling (manifests, check-in, guide
assignment, notes, availability) — that surface is fully functional without PII.
Set it `true` only when the app genuinely needs to contact customers or move
money, and only when the install is entitled to that data; the gateway is the
final authority and may still reject the request.

## Resources (accessor → methods)

- `getProductService()` — `getAllProducts()` (flat list of activities + add-ons;
  add-ons have `type === ADD_ON_PRODUCT_TYPE`); `Product.currency` carries the
  activity's ISO currency (empty for add-ons). Activities also expose the catalog
  fields `imageUrl`, `description`, and `meetingLocation`
  (`ProductMeetingLocation { summary, address, url }`) — all nullable, and
  `meetingLocation` is `null` when Peek reports no location detail (always `null`
  for add-ons). Each `Product.tickets[]` entry
  carries `minPrice`/`maxPrice` (`PricingMoney | null`, `null` for add-ons and
  when Peek reports no range); every `PricingMoney` includes a `displayPrice`
  string (e.g. `"$50.00"`) on values read back from the gateway.
- `getAccountUserService()` — `getAll()`, `getById(userId)`
- `getResourcePoolService()` — `getAll(mode?)`
- `getTimeslotService()` — `getForDay(productId, date, filter?)`, `getById(id)`,
  `setAvailability(...)`, `setNotes(...)`, `assignGuide({timeslotIds, guideIds, action})`
- `getResellerService()` — `getAllChannels(agentsPerChannel?)`
- `getPromoCodeService()` — `getAll()`, `create(input)`
- `getPricingService()` — `createEngine(input)`, `updateEngine(input)`,
  `deleteEngine(id)` (idempotent), `upsertOverrides(input)`, `clearOverrides(input)`.
  Primitives-only: caller builds the `UpsertOverridesInput` (segmentation,
  override `order`, `spotsTaken` bounds are the caller's job); service sends it
  as-is and returns the resolved `activityContexts`.
- `getDailyNoteService()` — `getToday()`, `update(note)`
- `getAvailabilityService()` — `getAvailabilityTimes({activityId, date, resourceOptionQuantities})`
- `getMembershipService()` — `getAll()`, `purchase(input)`
- `getBookingService()` — `getById(id, opts?)`, `searchByTimeRange(input)`,
  `searchByTimeslot(id, opts?)`, `getGuests(id)`, `getPaymentsOnFile(id)`,
  `appendNote(id, note, mode?)`, `setCheckinStatus(id, checkedIn)`, `cancel(id, notes?)`,
  `makePayment(input)`, `refund(input)`, `createInvoiceLink(id)`,
  `listAddons(id)`, `addAddon(id, {addonOptionId, quantity})`,
  `removeAddon(id, {addonOptionId, quantity})`, `create(input)`

## Sibling accessors (CNG, ACME — REST, not GraphQL)

Two brand-parallel accessors sit alongside `PeekAccessService` and share the same
auth/transport/UI plumbing. Both are **REST** and deliberately minimal today
(products only). Construct one per install, same config shape **minus `gatewayKey`**
(`installId`, `jwtSecret`, `issuer`, `apiUrl`). With `apiUrl` set, it is the REST
base and only the path is appended; the deprecated `baseUrl`/`appId` fall back to
the app-registry installations API default. `createAccessServiceForInstall` routes
`platform` `"cng"`/`"acme"` to these.

- `CngAccessService` — `getProductService().getAllActivities()` (short-form
  `getAllActivities()`) → `Activity[]` (`Activity`/`ActivityTicket` models).
  Errors surface as `CngApiError`.
- `AcmeAccessService` — `getProductService().getAllActivities()` (short-form
  `getAllActivities()`) → `AcmeActivity[]` (`AcmeActivity`/`AcmeActivityTicket`
  models). Errors surface as `AcmeApiError`.

All are exported from the package root `.`; REST paths and raw response shapes
stay internal.

## Input conventions (enforced in the service layer; violations throw plain Error)

- Booking ids normalized (lowercased, `-`→`_`): `B-ABC123` == `b_abc123`.
  Payment/refund need an id resolving to `b_…`.
- Quantities: positive-integer strings (`"1"`, `"2"`).
- Currency: 3-letter uppercase ISO (`"USD"`). Amounts: numeric strings (`"25.00"`).
- Payment source ids: `ps_…` or `cash/cash` | `custom/other` | `custom/voucher`.
  Payment ids (refunds): `pmt_…`.
- Idempotency key required on `makePayment`, `refund`, `create({markAsPaid:true})`.
- `create()` uses pre-resolved ids only (resolve via product + availability
  services); no free-text matching.

## Errors

- `AdminAccountRequiredError` (HTTP 418), `RateLimitError` (HTTP 429 after
  retries), `PeekGraphQLError` (`.graphqlErrors` holds the raw array — a
  resolver-level failure), `PeekHttpError` (a non-2xx HTTP status other than
  418/429 with no GraphQL `errors` — e.g. 401/404/5xx; carries `.statusCode`,
  `.url`, and raw `.body`; surfaced before JSON parsing so non-JSON error pages
  keep their status), `PiiAccessDisabledError` (a payment/booking-modification op
  was called without `fullCustomerAccess`), and the REST-sibling `CngApiError` /
  `AcmeApiError` — all importable; branch with `instanceof`. Token claim
  extraction never throws once the signature verifies: a missing `user` block
  gives `user: null`, and each user field (including `id`, the person's own id —
  not an account/partner id) is nullable, with `""`/`"null"` normalized to `null`.
- Plain `Error` for validation/precondition failures thrown before any request.

## Webhooks (booking + waiver + install)

Two pure-transform parsers plus one verify-and-parse call. The pure parsers need
no auth/network/`PeekAccessService`; accept the `{<key>:…}` envelope, a bare node,
or a JSON string; never throw on malformed input. Registration is done **once in
an external system** (App Store config), not from code.

- `parseBookingWebhook(body): Booking` — auto-detects guests/breakdown. Booking
  payload shape is defined by a GraphQL selection registered externally; paste
  the canonical maximal selection into `output_fields_gql_query`. That string is
  documented in `docs/webhooks.md` and pinned by a drift-guard test — it is NOT a
  runtime export.
- `parseWaiverWebhook(body, options?): Waiver` — maps the fixed `snake_case`
  `waiver_webhook_data` payload to the clean `Waiver` model. **No query to
  register** — just subscribe to the `agreement_signature_created` event. Takes
  the same `AccessOptions`; by default (`fullCustomerAccess` off) `guestName` and
  `fileUrl` are redacted — pass `{ fullCustomerAccess: true }` to keep them.
- `parseInstallWebhook(token, body, secret): InstallWebhook` — the install
  webhook delivers **two payloads at once**: a signed `app_registry_v2` JWT and a
  JSON body. This **verifies** the token (HMAC signature + expiry +
  `app_registry_v2` issuer + `Joken` audience — same checks as
  `verifyPeekAuthToken`, throwing the underlying `jsonwebtoken` error on failure,
  one `try/catch` → `401`) and merges both into one flat, JSON-safe
  `InstallWebhook`: `installId`, `accountId` (**also called the partner ID**),
  `accountName`, `platform`, `isTest`, `timezone`, `apiUrl`, `status`,
  `rawStatus`, `displayVersion`, `user` (nullable, for system-initiated events).
  The **JSON body is the source of the event data**; the fields it shares with
  the token (`installId`/`accountId`/`status`/`displayVersion`/`user`) fall back
  to the **verified token** when the body omits them. The token authenticates the
  whole delivery, so the body is trusted within a verified request. This webhook
  is the **only** source of `accountId`, `timezone`, and `apiUrl` in the package
  — no GraphQL read returns them; **persist them per install**. `status` and `platform`
  are **nullable**: a value this version does not recognise maps to `null` (wire
  value kept on `rawStatus`) rather than being coerced, because Peek does not
  redeliver a 2xx and a coerced status silently drops a lifecycle transition. Give
  both a `default:` branch that fails loudly. `token` is Peek's `x-peek-auth`
  request header value — pass it as-is, a `Bearer ` prefix is stripped for you.
  `secret` is the app's `jwtSecret`, app-wide, so it verifies fine on a brand-new
  install before any record exists. No query to register; just subscribe to the
  event.
  - **Deprecated / removed:** `verifyInstallWebhook(token, secret):
    InstallWebhookClaims` still verifies the token but is `@deprecated` — it reads
    only the token, missing the account name/platform/test flag. `parseInstallEvent`
    (the JSON-body-only parser) has been **removed**. Use `parseInstallWebhook`.

**Full guide + booking query-to-register: `docs/webhooks.md` (shipped).**

## UI components (`@peektravel/app-utilities/ui`)

Browser-only, framework-agnostic Web Components (Custom Elements, light DOM,
dependency-free) ported from the Peek Odyssey design system. The server library
above stays DOM-free. **Full guide: `docs/ui.md` (shipped). Authoritative
per-component contract: `dist/ui/index.d.ts` (TSDoc) — read via go-to-definition.**

Setup — importing the entry registers every `<ody-*>` element as a side effect:

```ts
import "@peektravel/app-utilities/ui";
import "@peektravel/app-utilities/ui/tokens.css";
import "@peektravel/app-utilities/ui/odyssey.css";
```

Conventions: scalar config = HTML **attributes**; rich data = JS **properties**
(`el.columns`/`el.data`, `el.formatDate`, `el.isDateDisallowed`; composites also
accept JSON-string attrs like `options='[…]'` / `tabs='[…]'`); output = bubbling
**`CustomEvent`s** (read `event.detail`); content = light-DOM children.

React 19: JSX props are set as DOM **properties**. Safe by design — every
getter-only accessor accepts assignment (registration adds a setter): reflected
props (`searchable`/`disabled`/`options`) reflect onto the attribute and take
effect; read-only state props (`isOpen`/`isVisible`) ignore the write (drive them
via a `ref`'s imperative methods). No `only a getter` crash. TS still types them
read-only — the setters are a runtime safety net.

Registration is idempotent (importing twice never throws). Lazy registration:
`odyssey.css` ships a `:not(:defined){visibility:hidden}` guard so un-upgraded
`<ody-*>` never flash as raw text (load the CSS eagerly), and `whenOdysseyReady()`
(`Promise<void>`) resolves once every imported element has upgraded — gate first
render on it. `registeredTags()` returns the registered tag list. A failed
dynamic import rejects at the `import()` call site.

Tags by tier (see `docs/ui.md` for attributes/events/examples per component):
- display: `ody-button`, `ody-tag`, `ody-alert`, `ody-card`, `ody-horizontal-divider`
  (1px rule with a default `margin-block: var(--gap16)`; `spacing="tight"|"none"`),
  `ody-status-dot`, `ody-message`, `ody-icon`, `ody-loading-spinner`, `ody-loading-bar`
- layout: `ody-empty-state`, `ody-breadcrumb`(+`-item`), `ody-stat-summary`(+`ody-stat`),
  `ody-inline-list`(+`-item`), `ody-list-item`, `ody-product-indicator`,
  `ody-toggle-button`, `ody-section-rows`/`-columns`(+items), `ody-two-column`(+parts),
  `ody-collapsible-section`, `ody-app-page-container` (required page wrapper for a
  settings UI — 868/1310px widths, `ody-page` container context, default responsive
  gutter; `flush` opts out)
- deprecated (kept, unchanged): `ody-divider` → use `ody-horizontal-divider` (the old
  one has zero margin); `ody-page-container` → use `ody-app-page-container` (the old
  one is full-bleed with no gutter). Migrate by renaming the tag.
- form: `ody-input`, `ody-inline-input`, `ody-search-input`, `ody-money-input`,
  `ody-percentage-input`, `ody-checkbox`, `ody-radio-button-group`, `ody-checkbox-group`
- interactive: `ody-accordion`, `ody-collapsible`, `ody-tabs`, `ody-copy-button`,
  `ody-check-in-status`, `ody-option`, `ody-split-button`, `ody-table-header`
- overlays: `ody-modal`, `ody-popover`, `ody-tooltip`, `ody-panel`,
  `ody-toast-host` (+ the `toast()` function)
- data/selection: `ody-dropdown-single`, `ody-dropdown-multi`, `ody-datepicker`, `ody-table`

Icons: themeable `<ody-icon name>` (inherits `currentColor`; discover via
`iconNames()`, extend via `registerIcon()`) and fixed-colour `<ody-brand-icon name>`
(`brandIconNames()`). Localization: `registerTranslation(lang, terms)` + DOM `lang`
(`<html lang>`/nearest ancestor), per-instance overrides like `close-label`. The
datepicker `value`/`change` stay ISO `yyyy-mm-dd`; display is `Intl`-localized
(`display-format` / `formatDate`). Not ported (use native/compose):
`nested-multi-select`, `location-autocomplete`, `filter-menu`(`-single`),
`accordion-checkbox`, `datepicker-with-presets`.

## Notes for consumers

- Install from the public npm registry: `npm install @peektravel/app-utilities`.
  No registry config or auth token needed. See README "Install".
- Public entry points: the package root `.` (server library) and `./ui`
  (+ `./ui/tokens.css`, `./ui/odyssey.css`). Everything else is internal — rely
  on those barrels, don't deep-import internal modules.
